head: 1e58780fbfeaaec8f1bdde05120b5f3dacc8bae7
title: A covered repo passed in URL or other non-canonical form silently gets the platform PAT.
reason: The PR description says "A URL, a third segment or a ./.. segment skips the provider tier" and the normalize_repo docstring says URLs are refused on purpose; also no call site uses the resolver yet.

head: 1e58780fbfeaaec8f1bdde05120b5f3dacc8bae7
title: A wall-clock bound in a unit test can fail on a slow or loaded CI runner.
reason: Speculative flakiness: the test docstring says the bounded pattern takes milliseconds, and the ~8M backtrack steps run in the regex engine's compiled code, far under the 0.5 s bound; nothing shows it actually gets close.

head: 06b90ae503e80213e8c3af657ed67c22f5312f03
title: The documented `rule_refused` remedy still says "share the agent", unlike the changed admin message.
reason: True that approvals.md:189 still says 'share the agent', but this is doc wording only; the actual 409 message in _rule_refused_message (ask_service.py:1244-1253) already gives the correct 'make sure ... can sign in' remedy.

head: 06b90ae503e80213e8c3af657ed67c22f5312f03
title: The troubleshooting remedy for a held credential entry leaves out the blocked and deactivated causes.
reason: Doc wording only: the troubleshooting line is less complete than approvals.md:162, but the runtime refusal messages and the main doc already name the correct remedy, so this is a docs-wording nit.

head: 06b90ae503e80213e8c3af657ed67c22f5312f03
title: Public `reachable_people` was removed without a replacement under that name.
reason: A search of src/ for `reachable_people` finds no matches; only the security reports mention its removal, so nothing can hit an AttributeError.

head: bb4c0e3ddba219c994fddf971198996b45819d79
title: A top-level `import psycopg` stops the whole test module loading under psycopg2.
reason: requirements.txt:37 pins psycopg[c]==3.3.6 and unittests/test_async_delete.py:20 already imports psycopg at module top, so a psycopg2-only setup is not supported and the import cannot fail.

head: 3e0d6cff2708c94a8440df4823469e1f53767cee
title: New refusal of a dimension role change is not part of #1507.
reason: The discussion says this 409 DIMENSION_HAS_CODES refusal was added to this PR on purpose as one of three fixes from the epic review; the finding only questions scope and names no defect.

head: 3e0d6cff2708c94a8440df4823469e1f53767cee
title: A failing language list now fails the job, and the list may not be the provider's source languages.
reason: getAvailableLanguages returns feature.config.availableLanguages, documented as 'Available target languages (for translation)' and checked against targetLanguage in translation-feature.js, so a French email in a company offering only en/nl targets loses its fr source and falls back to guessing.

head: 3e0d6cff2708c94a8440df4823469e1f53767cee
title: Unrequested change to the published `locale` template value, which may leave `lang` stale.
reason: The author announced this change in the discussion (#1505 fix), and the loop at lines 43-45 already sets values.locale = '' when the company's own locale dimension has nothing selected, so lang is not left stale.

head: 201c6dae4ca33fcafffe0cb02c793cb215a801e1
title: The new SDF_LZ4 branch takes over the return of the UE_IO branch, so IoStore jobs fall through.
reason: Patch lines 269-272 put the new `if ... == SDF_LZ4:` block between `ue_io_shaders(...)` and the context-line `return`, which now belongs to the SDF branch, so UE_IO jobs fall through to the rest of `scan_file_in`; the maintainer's review confirms this.

head: 3c71fe893496207bb5dccc8ebf015c5f7ba0ae1f
title: An unset belief_time may stop the lookup from finding existing annotations, so repeat posts create duplicates.
reason: `belief_time` is `nullable=True` with no default (annotations.py:25), so an annotation created without one is stored as NULL and the `== None` filter becomes `IS NULL`, which matches the stored row; the default this finding relies on does not exist.

head: 3c71fe893496207bb5dccc8ebf015c5f7ba0ae1f
title: `scalar_one_or_none()` can raise MultipleResultsFound on existing rows that match the new, wider key.
reason: Annotations with a NULL belief_time are created routinely (CLI data_add.py:1029-1036, 1058), and PostgreSQL's unique constraint lets NULLs repeat (data_sources.py:422 notes NULLS NOT DISTINCT is not used); the old lookup included `end`, so rows differing only in end could pile up, and the new lookup without `end` makes `scalar_one_or_none()` raise MultipleResultsFound.

head: 560786c37e3658457a0821b119d322bb767045bc
title: Battery level formula is not clamped to 0–100 %.
reason: The finding only holds if the shared file does not clamp, and it does: features/battery-voltage.yaml line 39 has a filter `std::min(100.0f, std::max(0.0f, x))` that keeps every level from the formula between 0 and 100 and leaves NAN unknown.

head: 92f784b94f218c58d45b481aba4a13723f51e298
title: Local `nativeThreadId` still holds the expired checkpoint's thread ID after it is dropped
reason: The local nativeThreadId is written back to the record only in onAccepted (line 1050). In turn.ts, onAccepted fires inside native.run at line 113, after onThread at line 107 has replaced the stale ID, and a failure before that point writes nothing back.

head: d8682e7a9af21ba8a4ff0946f3716ef442ccaea6
title: The usage insert takes the student only from the assessment instance, which can break group-assessment submissions.
reason: shared-question-usages.sql already handles team assessments: it LEFT JOINs team_users and uses coalesce(ai.user_id, tu.user_id) (line 30), and it filters `p.user_id IS NOT NULL` (line 58), so it never inserts a NULL user_id.

head: f82775f7eac6be8be96a0462803545b0a07bedf0
title: New automatic consent re-prompt for ordinary monitors
reason: The fresh-consent retry at portal.rs:445-447 replaces an outright error that already told the user to pick the monitor in the host dialog. It is a deliberate change with no failure, only a mismatch with the description.

head: f82775f7eac6be8be96a0462803545b0a07bedf0
title: Every switched-away monitor is parked, not only the shadowed PBP half
reason: The description's suspended pool pauses any monitor the viewer switches away from ("切出…时…pw_stream_set_active(false)"), and end() at lines 400-406 keeps only shadowed handles after a disconnect, so parking all switched-away monitors during a session is intended.

head: f82775f7eac6be8be96a0462803545b0a07bedf0
title: Lead/shadowed choice follows Mutter's logical-monitor order, which may not match the portal's restore order
reason: Whether xdg-desktop-portal-gnome matches monitors in the same order as Mutter's logical-monitor list is outside the repo, and the finding itself admits it could not check this.

head: f82775f7eac6be8be96a0462803545b0a07bedf0
title: A portal desktop stream with no input owner yet exits without streaming or logging anything.
reason: role.input is set at webrtc.rs:295 (`if desktop { *role.input.lock().unwrap() = Some(input.desktop_session()); }`) before stream.spawn at line 489, so owner is Some.

head: f82775f7eac6be8be96a0462803545b0a07bedf0
title: If `switch_screen` returns `Ok(None)`, the request carries on as if no screen change was asked for.
reason: switch_to can return Ok without calling publish (portal.rs:434, when the portal already captures that connector), giving Ok(None), but that needs the screen selection and the portal monitor to disagree, which recovery normally keeps in step, and the effect is minor.

head: dad629b193271731674b6d20b14ff23e5bf52bb8
title: `task_statuses` skips every task after a build that returned composition errors.
reason: When `composition_errors` is non-empty, the function returns `Err(RoverClientError::SubgraphBuildErrors{..})` at lines 211-227, before the `CheckWorkflowResponse` holding `task_summaries` is built, so the shortened list is never output as `task_statuses`.

head: b112503b1761cd1b7f02697ab23ef66c2ca19a75
title: Per-line grid opacity checks both axis styles instead of the line's own axis.
reason: The `grid_alpha` closure (plot.rs:6182-6185) is shared by both axes and checks both `grid_lines_style.0` and `.1`. `is_axis_style_entry` accepts `Automatic`, so `{Automatic, Directive[Red]}` leaves x unstyled. Even so, an x line with its own color then gets alpha 1.0 instead of the default 0.4.

head: b360ab9fd75765c7eac39d1be378a833ca8544ff
title: Quick toggles start helper runs that can finish in either order, so the panel can end up in the opposite state from the switch.
reason: glue.rs:404-412 starts a separate pkexec helper thread for every toggle and nothing orders them; panel_refresh_set ignores success, and helper::write (panel_refresh.rs:188-190) uses the same `.new` temp file for every run, so the race and the false rename failure both hold.

head: b360ab9fd75765c7eac39d1be378a833ca8544ff
title: At boot, `apply` stops waiting if Intel's driver hasn't bound yet, so PSR stays at the kernel default (on) and the switch is hidden.
reason: module.nix:811-812 orders the unit only after sys-kernel-debug.mount, nothing in the repo loads xe/i915 in initrd, and the loop at aizome-panel-refresh.rs:29 breaks immediately when intel_display() finds no bound driver, so a late-binding driver leaves PSR at its default (on) and the switch hidden.

head: 2666b3b115fb46f49408349fd4d101a2aea1856a
title: Quickstart code still asks for the removed 'Everett Mono' font.
reason: globals.css (and all of ui/src) no longer defines an 'Everett Mono' font-face; only the inline fontFamily strings at Quickstart.tsx:62/81/217/234 reference it, so these fall back to default monospace.

head: 2666b3b115fb46f49408349fd4d101a2aea1856a
title: Three provider brand colors were changed even though the PR says provider colors are left alone.
reason: Swapping three provider bg hex values for near-equivalent status fills is a cosmetic colour/description-mismatch nit with no functional failure.

head: 2666b3b115fb46f49408349fd4d101a2aea1856a
title: Unguarded decodeURIComponent can crash the whole app shell.
reason: The crash at AppShell.tsx:104 needs a malformed percent-escape in the path, which Next.js typically rejects before rendering; couldn't confirm for this version and the trigger is very unlikely.

head: 2666b3b115fb46f49408349fd4d101a2aea1856a
title: StatusBadge builds `badge-${tone}` class names that may not exist for every tone, such as `badge-yellow`.
reason: globals.css defines .badge-yellow (line 321), .badge-red (331), .badge-neutral (336) and .badge-green, covering every tone StatusBadge emits.

head: 2666b3b115fb46f49408349fd4d101a2aea1856a
title: Disabled styling may be lost when the buttons switch to `.btn` classes.
reason: globals.css:189 defines `.btn:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 0.5; }`, so disabled styling is preserved.

head: 2666b3b115fb46f49408349fd4d101a2aea1856a
title: Save button loses its disabled styling and size class.
reason: Base .btn sets height 28px and padding 0 8px (globals.css:171-172) and .btn:disabled dims it, so the Save button has both size and disabled styling.

head: f20ab5e83d94a55f133293cfa8f8e58de07cde65
title: Arrow UTF-8 bytes are checked against the database encoding, not decoded from UTF-8.
reason: imp_text_check copies the established pq_text_cell_ok policy (columnar_parquet_reader.c:1379-1380 also verifies against GetDatabaseEncoding without converting), and the approving reviewer already raised this exact LATIN1/EUC_JP point as a non-blocking follow-up for both readers, noting it is not a regression because the old code stored the bytes unconverted, which is not valid text in the database

head: bf16d5561ed62aceac55e9fd81976fd491459ffa
title: Coroutines created in Lua inherit the count hook and keep one budget across all later calls.
reason: environment.cpp:247-253 only opens base, table, string and math, never luaopen_coroutine, so scripts have no `coroutine.create`/`wrap`; the only lua_newthread in src is the startThread one in callback.h:66, which already clears the inherited hook.

head: a2669342ca17bf49ec71236f8f17750b511f9da4
title: Unrequested change to which secret the Studio CI job uses for credentials.
reason: The secret change is a deliberate commit of its own (a266934 "ci(studio): use STUDIO_READ_ACCESS_TOKEN in tests-studio.yml"); the finding only objects to scope and names no failure.

head: a2669342ca17bf49ec71236f8f17750b511f9da4
title: update_dataset_version now writes created_at for every caller, not just touch_reservation.
reason: catalog.py has no `created_at=` and no `**to_dict()` spread, so no caller is shown passing created_at except touch_reservation; the failure described is hypothetical.

head: a2669342ca17bf49ec71236f8f17750b511f9da4
title: New writer branch in insert_stored_rows is unused by the listing writer and changes shared behaviour.
reason: records.py:141 calls insert_stored_rows with column names that leave out sys__id, so the branch is used on purpose to give those rows writer ids; the finding names no failure.

head: 362c4ccfe64f7d0f590272ac9791a99db2fbe254
title: The version `sources` field is reused to store a version string, then parsed as a semver.
reason: The only code that writes a listing version's `sources` is listing.py:653 (`sources=version`), which always writes a version string; older listings came from `DataChain.save()`, which never passes `sources`, so it defaults to "" (catalog.py:1107), and the `if prev_ver.sources` guard skips the parse.

head: 6bc9e60c407b209d3ef8ea5dfa60ae40bbafd7df
title: Agg no longer gets the rows of each partition in the user's order.
reason: Agg's input query is rebuilt by `get_input_query` (dataset.py:630, `select(...).select_from(table)`) from a saved input table, then joined to the partition table (dataset.py:1090), so it carries no ORDER BY and the old `*query._order_by_clauses` was already empty: users lose no order they had before.

head: 6bc9e60c407b209d3ef8ea5dfa60ae40bbafd7df
title: `Partition` no longer sorts its query by partition, so it now relies on whatever `execute` does.
reason: Both callers that run `Partition` (dataset.py:802 and dispatch.py:80) pass `warehouse.dataset_select_paginated`, which always sorts by `(partition_id, sys__id)` (warehouse.py:180), and nothing in the repository overrides it; the unsorted `execute` the finding describes is only a guess.

head: 52e6865e8c440b5d60b8f638ddf519d69971a1c5
title: `self.url()` can cost an extra Hub request on every read that goes to the Hub.
reason: `PinnedHfFileSystem.url` (lines 187-197) overrides upstream and builds the URL with `hf_hub_url` from the resolved path, without calling `isdir`/`info`, so the extra `paths_info` request the finding describes does not happen.

head: 56e43481860ad807307b9c4672e942b79723693c
title: Adds a required native dependency and a subprocess SQLite writer that the column-projection request doesn't cover.
reason: This is a scope remark about the adbc dependency and the writer, which likely come from the stacked base PR (#2225 / a60df5a native Arrow ingestion); it names no failure.

head: 56e43481860ad807307b9c4672e942b79723693c
title: `save()` now renames the UDF output table straight into the dataset, which goes beyond column projection.
reason: This is a scope complaint ('goes beyond column projection'); it describes no concrete failure in save()'s rename path at lines 3250-3263.

head: 56e43481860ad807307b9c4672e942b79723693c
title: Every `apply_steps` now imports pyarrow, even for chains with no Arrow reader.
reason: pyarrow is a required dependency (pyproject `pyarrow>=22`), so the import happens once per process, and the per-row isinstance check costs nobody would notice; this is a perf nit with no defect.

head: 56e43481860ad807307b9c4672e942b79723693c
title: The Arrow fast path picks an arbitrary type from `kept`, which can disagree with the row path.
reason: codec.py:563-566 always builds `kept` as a one-element frozenset (`{str}` or `{py_type}`), so `next(iter(codec.kept))` always returns the same type.

head: 56e43481860ad807307b9c4672e942b79723693c
title: The child's stderr is piped but only read after the child dies, so a chatty child can deadlock the load.
reason: The deadlock needs the child to write more than 64 KB to stderr during a load, but the worker in `_run` never writes to stderr normally, so I can't tell whether ADBC or pyarrow warnings would ever fill the pipe.

head: 3a540fbf908c7c1b7ea824d25039200485247781
title: Changing the default delta key on GCS can break delta pipelines saved before this change
reason: Delta never stores or compares the previous run's key: `delta_key_changed_error` (delta.py:80) is raised only when a method overwrites a key column (datachain.py:2097, udf.py:972), and the source diff at delta.py:312-317 uses the current `spec.on`; old results still contain `file.path` and `file.version`, so the new default key still matches them.

head: 7bb007aecd91f0f859d1612b214123bdc427610f
title: Bump to diadata v1.4.714 may point at a release that doesn't exist yet or lacks a go.sum entry.
reason: The author's discussion says PR Validation creates the v1.4.714 release, the same flow #1309 used. Also, `cmd/http/restServer/go.sum` has never had a diadata entry, so the existing build doesn't depend on one and the missing entry is not a new failure.

head: 1ac4256d36330b7ba5ee9b29d9f3c8ab42ddfa3e
title: The joined title folder name no longer has any length limit.
reason: Line 45 `titles.map(slugify).join(TITLE_SEPARATOR)` cuts each title on its own but never cuts the joined folder name. Two 150-byte titles, or four 64-character ones, give a name past 255 bytes, which the old `sanitizeSegment(titles.join(...))` prevented.

head: 1ac4256d36330b7ba5ee9b29d9f3c8ab42ddfa3e
title: Slugifying test file paths lets different spec files share one step folder.
reason: run-step.ts:105 compares only `header.test` with the test title, so two spec files whose paths slugify to the same folder (`sign up.spec.ts` and `sign-up.spec.ts`) would share steps without an error. But it also needs the same describe and test titles in both files, which may be too rare to matter.

head: d6ac5fa3ede487e0ba6c5e86fb55ce6e8e72cea9
title: Concurrent PUTs to the same key can share a temp file name.
reason: Line 22 builds the temp name from only `${file}.${process.pid}.${Date.now()}.tmp`, so two PUTs of the same key in the same millisecond on one server would share a temp file, and the failure the finding describes can happen; but it needs two uploads in the same millisecond on a store described as being for tests and a single Node server, so it is unclear whether it matters in practice.

head: b7b435eb2124bf140b33e3bddae3025a235240ba
title: The linking -en- rule also removes final stress from Latinate -endeer/-enseer verbs.
reason: L20 (line 4) includes d and s, so agendeer/recenseer match the more specific `@CenL20) ee (r_ I` over `@) ee (r_ 'I`, and nl_list has no entries for these verbs (only agenda).

head: b7b435eb2124bf140b33e3bddae3025a235240ba
title: `model` has no guard for `modellen`/`modelleren`, unlike `hotel`, `tabel` and `snel`.
reason: hotel (line 618) and snel (line 1156) have a `(le` guard before `(l@P5`, but model (lines 861-862) has none, so modellen/modelleren match `model (l@P5` and are split; nl_list has no modell* entries.

head: b7b435eb2124bf140b33e3bddae3025a235240ba
title: Common adjectives derived from compounds now get first-element stress (oorspronkelijk, huishoudelijk).
reason: oorspronkelijk matches `oor (C@P3` (line 969), huishoudelijk matches `huis (C@P4` (line 602) and spreekwoordelijk matches `spreek (C@P6` (line 1169), and none of them is in nl_list or has a guard rule.

head: 9d387ace23e145ab0d210aee5e8ac31295c4dc4d
title: Integrated devices without an energy collector now always report 0 charged energy.
reason: configureChargerType (loadpoint.go:508-511) always sets chargeMeter before the `chargeMeter != nil && collector != nil` check at line 306, and newLoadpoint always passes a collector; the authors removed the fallback on purpose in e75c900 because the only nil-collector instance (config UI) never runs.

head: 9d387ace23e145ab0d210aee5e8ac31295c4dc4d
title: The translation key `main.loadpoint.todayEnergy` may not exist.
reason: The key main.loadpoint.todayEnergy exists in all i18n files (e.g. i18n/en.json:1707 "todayEnergy": "Today") and Loadpoint.vue:80 already uses it.

head: 3d9aa25dc2adcad26de3112d48dc8eeea49802cb
title: Ensure moves the source to whichever account was noted last, so deleting that account orphans the source.
reason: connector_accounts is unique only on (connector_id, external_account_id), so two connectors in one org can share an AWS account; Ensure's ON CONFLICT (lines 94-98) re-points the source to the last-noted account, and deleting that connector cascades to its account, whose ON DELETE SET NULL link then excludes the source from LoadNextDueForUpdateSkipLocked while the other account is still live.

head: 3d9aa25dc2adcad26de3112d48dc8eeea49802cb
title: cloudfront is imported directly but listed as `// indirect`.
reason: The `// indirect` marker on go.mod line 105 is a bookkeeping detail that `go mod tidy` fixes, not a defect.

head: 3d9aa25dc2adcad26de3112d48dc8eeea49802cb
title: Backfill links and schedules every AWS connector account, including disabled ones.
reason: connector_accounts (migrations 20260921T155710Z and 20261012T114837Z) has no enabled, disabled or revoked state, so the backfill has no disabled accounts to filter and no status to tie-break on.

head: df7f8a828ebb1a2da03fc86c570ad4bbffa53798
title: Signed 32-bit mul_shift_right with q > 32 may still fall back to a 64-bit multiply.
reason: lower_mul_shift_right (FindIntrinsics.cpp:1563-1568) rewrites q > bits as mul_shift_right(a, b, a.type().bits()) — that is q == 32 even for signed types — followed by a shift, so the new q == 32 branch catches it; full_q = 31 is only used for the q < full_q case.

head: 062992661ca19a00e624c37d36c2329221ac207d
title: Room refresh failures are dropped with no log and no signal to peers.
reason: The finding is mainly about a missing log, which is not a defect. The failure loop it describes needs an error that keeps happening and is speculative: if `FetchChanges` fails it returns before `docMu` is taken (hub.go:631), and the snapshot rebuild runs outside the lock in `FetchChanges` (persist.go:438-449), so only a merge of changes the document mostly already holds runs under the lock.

head: d49c98bc271cb1a94e8e138057252ef0c09513c8
title: Extensionless documents with a dot in the name are now skipped silently.
reason: Line 348 checks `filepath.Ext(found) != ""`, and `IsMarkdownFile` only accepts the six Markdown extensions, so a dotted extensionless name like `release-1.2` gets `.2` and is skipped silently, which breaks the PR's claim that extensionless files behave as before.

head: c196d53b7f6d604bb88d4e17f0fbffd7e0de1ce6
title: AccentVars switch the focus outline, expand icon, filter focus border and selection fill to --primary, which the PR says it does not change.
reason: Commit c196d53 ('shadcn theme: use the page's --primary where the default theme uses its accent') deliberately adds AccentVars and its test; the mismatch is only with stale PR description text, not a defect.

head: c196d53b7f6d604bb88d4e17f0fbffd7e0de1ce6
title: Inlining default-theme values breaks user overrides of the variables they referenced.
reason: Before this PR these 14 vars were only declared on :root (theme-default.css.ts globalStyle(':root', LightTheme)), so their var() references resolved there and overrides set on the grid never reached them. Build-time inlining is the stated intent ('computed ... at build time, so they can't drift'), and the dark values use shadcn's --border on purpose.

head: 22a6bf6bca3577835e0f0ba6129a683a6ff56612
title: Clearing the current repo before startup empties the repo list, so Desktop opens the demo graph instead of the user's other graphs.
reason: get-repos uses db-persist/get-all-graphs, which concatenates the on-disk ipc "getGraphs" list with <list-db results (persist.cljs lines 33-40), so repos still contains the other graphs when <list-db returns [].

head: 22a6bf6bca3577835e0f0ba6129a683a6ff56612
title: The current repo is compared to raw `getGraphs` names, which may not use the same format.
reason: The getGraphs handler returns common-graph/get-db-based-graphs, which maps every dir name through canonicalize-db-version-repo (graph.cljs line 139), so names are full logseq_db_ repo URLs in the same form as the current repo.

head: 22a6bf6bca3577835e0f0ba6129a683a6ff56612
title: `restore-and-setup!` now rethrows graph-absent errors, which can break callers other than startup.
reason: A repo-wide search shows restore-and-setup! is called only from <restore-or-demo! and <open-startup-repo! (plus tests), and both catch graph-absent errors, so no other caller can get an unhandled rejection.

head: 377bea9de162116a94dda6948e872e3130682304
title: Rollback now reverses user txs while later :fix txs on the same entities stay applied, so the reversal can be left half done.
reason: Reversing an inserted block retracts the whole entity: reverse-tx-data runs replace-attr-retract-with-retract-entity-v2 (normalize.cljs:31), which turns the :block/uuid retract into :db/retractEntity, and reverse-history-action! (apply_txs.cljs:1150) extends it to descendants, so the fix's order is removed too and no orphan remains; reversed moves overwrite the single-valued order and repair-appli

head: e3b1d6c78b46026415423cc76ad5abc3d73a5ce4
title: `droppedAsEmpty` may be left unused after removing the lookahead, which would break the build.
reason: `droppedAsEmpty` is still called at responses.go:6274 (`... || droppedAsEmpty(&m)`), so removing the lookahead leaves it in use and the build does not break.

head: e488295eea0120f6a2c50db1d88be7ec59a8a70b
title: Reads after cleanup() now fail with ErrStreamClosed instead of reaching the upstream.
reason: Every caller runs the cleanup only after it has finished reading: by `defer stopIdleTimeout()` in each provider, in the `cleanup()` closures in `largeresponse.go` (called after `ReadAll` or on `LargeResponseReader` close) and from `Stream.complete` in `relay/stream.go` (on EOF or Close), so nothing reads after cleanup.

head: e488295eea0120f6a2c50db1d88be7ec59a8a70b
title: Each zero-byte Read now restarts the idle deadline, so a stream that keeps returning (0, nil) never times out.
reason: `startRead` (lines 4348-4353) does reset the deadline on every Read, so an endless run of (0, nil) reads would never time out. But the wrapped readers here (fasthttp/net/http bodies, gzip) do not return that pattern, and bufio callers stop after 100 empty reads with `io.ErrNoProgress`, so it is unclear the trigger can happen.

head: 9a8525417cb6d3f660a98e5080864a1eb8320fac
title: Test reads the port and makes the login call in one return statement, but Go does not fix their order.
reason: Line 636 `return gotPort, runner.authLogin(...)` reads a variable that the call itself sets via the OpenBrowser closure; the Go spec orders only calls left-to-right and leaves the variable read's timing unspecified, so the test relies on current gc behaviour.

head: 52bdad9bd327be821456a2af43d67e96baf24a3e
title: A retried save after a partial failure loses the fact that the router was turned on.
reason: The failure path holds. withSavedRouting (utils line 97) adds `enabled` to the baseline once the routing PUT succeeds, so if the name PUT then fails, the retry leaves `enabled` out of `toSend.routing`. Line 146 then sets turnedOn to false, so the user gets the plain 'saved' toast and onSaved does not switch to the overview, even though this sheet turned the router on.

head: c1709d7d5c572c6ea2d55f13c10002a81446fab0
title: The shared mint limit lets anyone lock a chosen IP, or a whole site, out of login.
reason: get_the_user_ip() trusts the rightmost X-Forwarded-For entry by default (functions.php:3985-3991). Once that IP's shared bucket is full, login_CAPTCHA returns early without captcha fields (3718-3720) and CAPTCHA_CHECK rejects the login (3755). So forged REST requests can lock a chosen IP out of login; the author's trade-off only addressed spoofing to bypass the limit.

head: c1709d7d5c572c6ea2d55f13c10002a81446fab0
title: Errors the user can act on are now replaced with a generic "try again" message.
reason: The PR description (item 8) and the code comment at theme-plus.php:226 say every WP_Error branch, including core errors that carry data, returns the generic message on purpose.

head: 9cefcf0a973941e775f1d9fc62dc303f1ffe8d00
title: Focus-return change not covered by the PR description.
reason: The author's discussion reply says getReturnElement now skips elements inside the closing popup to fix the MenuRoot.triggerless failure caused by the new unmount order, so the change is needed and explained; the rest only objects to the PR description.

head: 591d42add1773b5667e9db8e19f3e75954767fa3
title: `/ci` runs fork pull-request code with a `contents: write` token.
reason: pkgdown.yaml lines 14, 34-38 and 53-55: an `issue_comment` run holds a `contents: write` GITHUB_TOKEN (also exported as GITHUB_PAT), checks out `refs/pull/N/merge` and builds the PR's package and site, so PR code runs with a token that can push. The ci commits (b89ab2b..e943b80) are part of this PR.

head: 591d42add1773b5667e9db8e19f3e75954767fa3
title: Unrelated CI trigger rewrite stops pull requests from being checked on push.
reason: The new comment at lines 9-10 says on purpose that 'pushes to a PR branch no longer start CI', so this is a deliberate policy change; saying it is out of scope for the PR does not show a defect.

head: 591d42add1773b5667e9db8e19f3e75954767fa3
title: The approval gate does not check who reviewed the PR.
reason: Line 31 is right that the review path does not check `review.author_association`, but forked-PR review runs get a read-only token, and before this PR every push ran CI anyway, so the only impact is unwanted CI runs.

head: 591d42add1773b5667e9db8e19f3e75954767fa3
title: The status is reported on a head SHA that may not be the code that was tested.
reason: Line 73 saves `head.sha` before the checkout at line 88, which fetches the moving `refs/pull/N/merge` ref after the macOS brew installs. A push in that window gets its result posted to the older SHA, which can mark a commit green that was never tested.

head: 591d42add1773b5667e9db8e19f3e75954767fa3
title: `startsWith(body, '/ci')` also matches other comments.
reason: `startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/ci')` on line 31 matches any maintainer comment starting with '/ci' (e.g. '/cite'), and unlike the review path the `/ci` path has no main/master base check, so stacked PRs also run.

head: 3e29ad7128ee3b845fd40213756fe109628abf9f
title: A queued card arriving at a full live store is dropped from persistence straight away.
reason: LIVE_LIMIT is 100 (Store.js:150) and only first-run cards use --queue, so a full store at first login is very unlikely; and a queued card sits at the bottom of the stack, so trimming it with `slice(-LIVE_LIMIT)` is the same 'oldest go' rule that already drops the bottom card of an ordinary full stack.

head: 2effbabbe3f229419378684ac394ca0f77d9daae
title: Right-clicking a state while its menu is open moves the time cursor instead of opening the menu again.
reason: Line 422 sets interact_pos to None while the menu is open, so hovered_phase is None and a new secondary click takes the 'remove target / clicked_time' branch, moving the cursor instead of reopening the menu.

head: 2effbabbe3f229419378684ac394ca0f77d9daae
title: "Jump to start of state" goes through `f64`, so large timestamps lose precision.
reason: Line 985 casts start_time to f64, which is lossy for nanosecond timestamps above 2^53, and time_real.rs:92 shows `impl From<i64> for TimeReal` exists, so an exact conversion was available.

head: 47d3b1abd28f6755979c52396960cac45e77cb92
title: Partition shutdown is turned into a generic storage error.
reason: Line 86 maps the closed-partition error to `StorageError::OperationalError`, the same way the store already handles a refused submission to its own executor (`partition_store.rs:554` `.spawn(read).map_err(|_| StorageError::OperationalError)?`). `from_journal_reader` only wraps it as an ordinary `JournalReader` error, and the finding shows no visible harm from a retry while the partition shuts down

head: 28328dfa73ee2360ed587c64f6756d5dc590223e
title: ForType leaks the pairing it built when it then throws ArgumentException.
reason: Release() only calls Side.Complete(), which clears dictionaries and calls SymbolKeyBuilder.Release() (Reset(); _scratch = []); nothing is pooled, so a pairing dropped after the ArgumentException is simply garbage-collected and nothing leaks.

head: 9bdc5f1c645e87ec01540cf90f9808663e883c12
title: Expulsion warning text colour is still hard-coded to white.
reason: Line 12 still hard-codes `color: #fff`, but its background is now the themeable `var(--warn-3-bg)`. common.css defines no foreground variable for warn 3 (only `--warn-fg: #000`), so a theme can't change this text colour, which is exactly what this PR is meant to allow.

head: 5e7f5f9b138c5afbbc164cfbb58b5deebf84283f
title: Ported total goes up by two though only one game was added.
reason: The checklist entries run from line 11 to line 114, which is 104 lines, so `44 / 104` is right; the author's comment also says the list was recounted and upstream's 102 was one short.

head: 5e7f5f9b138c5afbbc164cfbb58b5deebf84283f
title: Every vertex shader is paired with the same pixel shader, c1a608e6add64c26.
reason: The only reader of shader_pairs.tsv is vs_pad in dmsh_build.py (lines 561-578), which only pads vertex outputs with (0,0,0,1) for Metal linking, so a single pixel key causes at most harmless padding; the 16:9 device check shows cars and roads drawing correctly.

head: f813c963b10fc9796fe585780a90d291cba7c35c
title: Merged initialState is a new object on every render, so Renderer may apply the saved filters again over the user's choice.
reason: useOpenUIState.ts:164-165 compares initialState by its JSON content (storeInitKeyRef), not by reference, so a new object with the same content made on each render is skipped and does not overwrite the user's choice.

head: f813c963b10fc9796fe585780a90d291cba7c35c
title: The restored state is checked against the version only once and is still passed after the version on screen changes.
reason: restoredRef checks the version only once and is reset only on [reads, id]. When a new version changes stateDeclarations, the key at useOpenUIState.ts:164 changes, and store.initialize (store.ts:86-91) writes the old version's saved state over the current values.

head: 8be082fbfeccf42c67a9414c7d628b0d3576d2e9
title: A refreshing compact Kpi tile now only anchors the shimmer if the sheen is a direct child of the tile.
reason: CompactKpi.tsx line 30 places <StateFrame compact> directly inside the .openui-dashboard-kpi-compact section, and StateFrame's refreshing branch returns a fragment, so the Sheen is a direct child and `:has(> .openui-dashboard-sheen)` matches; the data-compact rules in metrics.styles.ts only style the icon, the title and the loading skeleton, none of which the refreshing state draws.

head: 7408bb3f2750867b003e15fba47eef3e528a5571
title: Leftover inert-statement records from a failed load or non-file compile get reported against a later, unrelated load.
reason: `report_inert_statements` runs only after `setup_call_cleanup` returns normally (filereader.pl:32), and `check_statement` asserts `inert_statement/2` for every compile, including `process_metta_string`. So facts left by a failed load or a string load are retracted and reported, or thrown under `--strict`, by the next unrelated outermost file load.

head: 7408bb3f2750867b003e15fba47eef3e528a5571
title: `data` erasure lives only in constrain_args, so clauses compiled with ConstrainArgs=false keep the literal `(data ...)` head.
reason: Specialized clauses are compiled from `fun_meta(ArgsNorm, ...)`, which stores `Args1`, the head arguments after `constrain_args` (translator.pl:99-107; specializer.pl:55-58), and `stage_function_clauses` recompiles those same stored terms. So the `data` marker is already erased in specialized heads.

head: e958f3680edf514cba8c45cce441f6a78cf72c8c
title: Action samples likely won't compile in a project with ImplicitUsings turned on.
reason: The comment on line 47 says `using System;` makes `Action<>` ambiguous. A `global using System;` from ImplicitUsings, which the standard Umbraco project template turns on, imports `System.Action<T>` and `System.Action<T1,T2>` at the same level, so `: Action<ActionResult>` and `: Action<SendPeopleSettings, ActionResult>` fail with CS0104, and nothing in the repo shows a different build setup.
